The gen-1 bake stamps `memory_units` and `disk_gb` on the pool row it inserts (mngr-internal `new-fleet-phase-2`, slice-fleet cutover phase 2), now that the connector's migration 039 makes both columns NOT NULL. A gen-1 row's `disk_gb` is the size the machine's data disk will have after the gen-2 cutover (the gen-1 disk plus the 16 GiB gen-2 base); `compute_server_slice_sizing` reports both values.

- The per-box usage sum (`server` fit checks) reads `memory_units` / `disk_gb` directly instead of counting NULL rows at the default size.

- `server prep` on a gen-2 box now re-stages the guest image whenever its customization changed, not only when the qcow2 is absent: the staged image carries a marker with the sha256 of the image URL plus the `virt-customize` script (docker/containerd/gVisor pins, daemon and containerd config), and a mismatching or missing marker triggers a re-stage on the next prep. Deleting the image by hand is no longer needed after a customization change. Gen-1 boxes keep presence-only staging (retired by the cutover).

- Box-management dial resolution (the onetun userspace WireGuard tunnel behind every operator box SSH) is now single-flight: concurrent threads dialing the same box -- `pool destroy` at its default concurrency of 8, the bake, `teardown-slices` -- share one tunnel instead of each spawning their own with the same operator identity, which made the box's WireGuard flip sessions between them and dropped SSH sessions mid-destroy. `--max-concurrency 1` is no longer needed as a workaround.

- `server sweep-ci-slices` now sweeps gen-2 boxes too: it reads each box through the box generation's slice client (the same observations the orphan reaper uses) instead of parsing lima's on-disk layout, destroys stale `ci-*` VMs (running or not) and reclaims CI data disks whose VM is already gone. Its 4 h threshold and the orphan reaper's 2 h guard are now defined side by side in `mngr_imbue_cloud`'s `bare_metal.py`, and the deployment-tests orchestrator's Modal-env sweep reads the same 4 h constant.
